description: Set, correct or retire a limit on how many sessions this solet runs at once. A limit is a selector, a whole number of sessions at once, the user's words and an optional end time. The selector is the same one a model cell rule uses: provider, runtime, model_family_prefix, model and effort combine with AND, absent dimensions are wildcards, and {} means every session. Every limit that matches a session must hold before the solet starts it. A limit of 0 starts nothing new while work already running finishes. A limit past its ends_at no longer applies and reads as lapsed, but stays listed until someone retires it. Only sessions the solet itself started are counted, so a session a person started by hand is never counted and never refused. A limit counts sessions at once and nothing else, and it names no asker and no project. action is set (the default, writing revision 1 of a new limit), correct (replaces the whole limit, so an omitted ends_at clears the end time) or retire (ends the limit; to bring it back, set it again as a new limit, the retired one stays in the history). A nonblank reason is always required. correct and retire take limit_id and expected_revision, the revision you read with list_session_limits. Anyone may call: no role or identity is checked, and the calling principal is recorded as set_by (empty when the call carries none) as advisory history. Revisions are append-only; nothing is edited in place. An ends_at already past is kept with a warning.
embedding_description: Put a ceiling on how many sessions the solet runs at once, for example at most two codex sessions or zero to start nothing new while running work finishes, in the user's own words with an optional end time, then correct the number or retire the limit when it no longer applies.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: limit, the revision just written with its selector, sessions, words, ends_at, lapsed, set_by and set_at; limits, every active limit oldest first; warnings, for example when ends_at is already past so the limit applies to nothing.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Say the limit in the user's words and its number, and say whether it has lapsed. A limit of 0 means nothing new starts while running work finishes. Mention that sessions started by hand are not counted.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Pass the returned limit_id and revision as limit_id and expected_revision to a later correct or retire. To see every revision, call list_session_limits.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Typed StateManagementInterface session limit table; one or two rows per call, written in one transaction. No session is started, stopped or counted by this call, and no network or deployment action is taken.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: parameter_invalid: a field is missing or malformed; supply a selector object (empty means every session) using only provider, runtime, model_family_prefix, model and effort, a whole number sessions of 0 or more, nonblank words and reason, an ISO-8601 ends_at with a UTC offset, and action set, correct or retire; correct and retire also need limit_id and expected_revision. stale_limit: the limit is not active at that revision, because someone corrected or retired it first; nothing was written, so call list_session_limits and decide again from what is active. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound on this solet; restore the binding and repeat the call.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: parameter_invalid: fix the named field and repeat the call; nothing was written. stale_limit: call list_session_limits, take the current limit_id and revision, and repeat the correction or retirement only if it still applies. state_service_unavailable: restore the state service binding and repeat the call; setting the same limit twice makes two limits, so list first when unsure whether the first call landed.
